correctness.rationale: Every strict gcd chain of 3q has at most two drops because 3 and q are distinct primes. The standard characteristic-sequence conductor formula and exact admissible bounds separate the two-generator branch and the d=3,q triple branches. Necessity follows from the q congruence class and the lower and upper bounds; sufficiency follows because the d=3 intervals span [6q,(3q-1)(3q-2)] with all and only residues 0 and 2 modulo six, and U_k-L_(k+1)>=3q-1. The 0 and 3q-1 exceptions follow from a=1,2, and a=3 is impossible. Cardinality arithmetic is exact. Complete enumerations for q=7,13,19,31,37 agree with the symbolic spectrum; an independent Apéry shortest-path engine checks q=7,13 and a sample at q=19. These finite checks are supporting evidence only.

value.rationale: The exact attainable-conductor set for infinitely many odd non-prime-power Abhyankar–Moh degrees is a natural Frobenius-spectrum invariant directly motivated by the explicit odd-degree problem in arXiv:2209.04232v1. The two-residue filling law, sharp low gap, endpoint and closed cardinality are global structural information absent from per-degree enumeration or the general extremal bound. The q=5 counterexample shows a genuine arithmetic boundary. No generalization to arbitrary odd degrees is asserted.
